Background

eufyMake E1 raised nearly $47M on Kickstarter and entered customer delivery.

As customers began using the product, feedback revealed friction across the journey from design to physical print.

After two iterations, 3.0 focused on helping new users print with confidence, clarity, and efficiency.

In partnership with my mentor, I conducted journey audits, user interviews, and VOC analysis to diagnose the end-to-end printing experience and identify the highest-impact barriers and sort them in layers.

App 2.0 UX Optimization

-My Role-

Conducted a focused UX audit on the printing setup workflow, systematically reviewing key task flows and interaction issues.
Identified major usability pain points and proposed targeted design improvements to enhance operational clarity and overall efficiency.

2025

Solution Approach

A top-down system redesign strategy was adopted, which follows the Garrett UX Five-Plane Model to structure the redesign.

　Why

　What

How

Background

User feedback indicates a low recommendation rate for the current app，particularly regarding the printing workflow experience. Among all stages, the Printing Setup process was identified as the most critical pain point.

To fundamentally improve usability, increase operational efficiency, and better align with the printer’s hardware capabilities, this project focuses on deep optimization of the Printing Setup editor.

Strategy Layer

Define the product role and core value

Scope Layer

Clarify core user tasks and primary workflows

Structure Layer

Optimize information architecture and interaction logic

Surface Layer

Enhance visual presentation and user feedback

Four Steps to Solve the Problem

🤓

Through four progressive layers of redesign, the solution systematically addresses unclear positioning and disjointed workflows, building a printing experience that is clear, efficient, and controllable.

Step 1: Define the Core Positioning and Primary Task Model

As the mobile control hub within the UV printing ecosystem, the mobile experience serves as an extension of the web and desktop platforms. It is not designed for complex creative production. Instead, it enables users to turn ideas into printed output quickly and reliably in mobile scenarios.
